sources.citation: Crosse-Upcott, A.R.W. 1956. The social structure of the KiNgindo-speaking peoples. PhD thesis, University of Cape Town. 562+xxxiv pp. (OpenUCT handle 11427/23194; 708-page scan with scanned layer)
sources.note: Ethnographic thesis; only incidental remark, about kiNgindo dialects generally (pp. 26-27, PDF pp. 30-31): 'the Ngindo practice of accentuating the first syllable of the stem, as opposed to the penultimate'. Appendix A pp. iv.c-iv.d (PDF pp. 680-681) treats 'kiNdwewe' (archaic, one informant, Hassani Mzigo of Malinyi) and says it may be 'a distinct language, standing apart from the recognised Ngindo dialects'; all listed dialects 'with the exception of kiMbunga and kiNdwewe obviously belong to the same language'.
